The court will most likely choose **B**: the defendant's bare testimony that he kept the records regularly does not establish the trustworthiness of the computer-generated data, so a greater foundation is required. Option A states only one element of the business-records exception, and the defendant has not shown the others, such as that the entries were made by someone with knowledge at or near the time of the events. Options C and D are wrong because the defendant's availability as a witness does not remove the hearsay problem, and no reliability of the computer process has been shown.

CONFIDENCE: 72
